sessions.title: Session 3
sessions.lede: The second escape map plays through to its level change, and the last escape map gets through the flings and the catwalk into GLaDOS's chamber, then redirects rockets into her and burns two of her four cores.
landed: The rocket turret's timing and damage were measured in the original: first shot at 6.9 s, then one every 6 s, 550 u/s, lethal. Its rockets go through portals, it sees you through breakable glass, and it can turn a full circle.
Tube boxes take path_track's alternate path and spit out the cube, and the escape fan isn't solid, both as in the original.
You duck when you come out of a wall portal and stand up after a floor fling. A cube you're carrying stays in your hands through that duck.
Pointing at a door and pressing use now works, and so do look triggers.
Rocket blasts damage GLaDOS, and her cores burn in the incinerator.
sessions.regression: The wrap-up allplay first showed regressions in a02, a03, a06, a10, a13 and a15. The new duck at a wall portal had made you drop a carried cube and had undone the aim a10 needed for its lift; look triggers closed a06's fling-pillar doors while you looked down into the pit; a03's wall portal sat off the energy ball's path; and the new train code was grabbing a13's ball catchers and placing them rotated wrong. Those are fixed at d7b1478. A second allplay at 9:41–9:49 AM EST reached every level change except a07, which stopped short before this session too, and escape_02, which ends after the second core burns.
remains: GLaDOS's last two cores and the ending.
A route through a11 that survives turret damage, so ?damage=1 can become the default.
The hold-distance 81 change, parked because the playthrough scripts are tuned around 56.

sessions.title: Session 1
sessions.lede: An oracle was built from the original Portal (the native Linux build, driven through its own console) and the port was measured against it overnight. Walk, jump, duck, flings, cube size and +use reach were brought into line, and the playthroughs reached a11, with a13 underway.
landed: Movement (22 metrics on a09's floor): walk 150 against a previous 175, now 150. Running jump speed 225 against 175, now 225. Air strafe cap 60 against 30, now 60. Duck eye 90% at 0.345 s against 0.18 s, now matched. Running jump distance 116.6 against 116.6.
Floor-to-floor flings, which used to come back up 37–41 units too high, now match the drop height.
Floor-to-wall fling speed was still 2–5% high at the end of the session. A fix that got it to 400.0 / 527.3 / 627.3 broke a10 and was left uncommitted; it landed in session 2.
Cubes take their size from the model hull (±20.25 for metal_box), not a fixed ±12.
+use reach follows the SDK's FindUseEntity (80 units, hull sweeps, cone 0.8).
Glass takes no portal. Cleansers fizzle shots across them. Template cubes go to their own offsets.
The held cube follows the SDK grab controller more closely; hold distance stayed at 56, against about 81 in the original.
remains: a13's ball catchers and lifts, a14, and the escape maps (taken up in session 2).
The wall-fling height and the speed fix without breaking a10.
Held distance 81.
box_dropper's cover and prop_dynamic solidity.

sessions.title: macOS canvas and known no-ops
sessions.lede: On the hosted preview, Gabriel's Mac showed a00's floor button and the cube on it black except for their self-lit strips. The WebGL canvas is now opaque, which fixed it. env_tonemap_controller and logic_autosave inputs are registered as known no-ops.
landed: The cause was the canvas: model materials keep their $selfillum mask in the base texture's alpha, the opaque passes wrote it into an alpha-channel drawing buffer, and the page composited that buffer as premultiplied, which macOS shows as black. 71% of the pixels over the button and cube had alpha under 250. The context is now alpha: false; renders are byte-identical here and every pixel reads 255.
Harness additions: assert, PCTL_GL=mesa, and FILES_DIR, used while trying to reproduce the black models.
Over the first 20 s of a08 to escape_02 the only unhandled inputs were env_tonemap_controller and logic_autosave. They are registered as no-ops (LDR renderer, no saves).
web/ was also bumped to Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.87 and Effect 4.1.4, matching Horizon.
sessions.regression: These commits were merged to main as pull request #5 at 6:08 PM EST on 22 Nov (c26bacf), which was the tip of origin/main until the oracle work.
remains: game.ts still calls io.cancel?.() on choreo Cancel/Stop, but IO has no cancel, so pending outputs of a cancelled scene still fire.
v_hands.vtf still 404s: the material points at a path the game does not ship.
sessions.playthroughNote: No new playthrough was run this session; the work was a preview bug and a survey of unhandled inputs.

sessions.title: Animation session
sessions.lede: A five-hour session to stop judging animations from single screenshots. The harness can now record tick-by-tick mp4s, and the animation pipeline was brought in line with the public SDK 2013 rules. Floor turrets, the first-person gun, GLaDOS's cores, a10's lifts and a06's fling pillars all landed here. Merged to main as pull request #1 on 21 Nov.
landed: The animation pipeline follows the SDK rules: blend grids over pose parameters, delta and autoplay layers, 0.2 s sequence cross-fades, long sequences read from .ani sections, and client animation events, so elevator doors and the box dropper play their sounds on the right frame.
The first-person portal gun is drawn with its draw, fire, fizzle, pickup and release sequences.
Floor turrets deploy, aim, fire, search and tip over, and security cameras track the player.
GLaDOS's cores and the energy-ball catcher's ball ride their parent's attachment instead of floating in place.
$selfillum no longer turns a10/a14's lift platforms and turrets white.
Energy balls keep their modelled side to the viewer instead of showing a sliver.
a10's telescoping lifts sink all the way instead of stopping 128 units over the pit, riding them no longer throws the player up, and a06's fling pillars start where Hammer put them.
Portal shots slide off no-portal faces as well as edges. Cubes ride moving trains. Named lights switch their light styles, env_shake shakes the view, and func_noportal_volume takes its inputs.
Falling onto a floor portal keeps the fall speed. Before that fix the floor behind the hole stopped the player and every fling came out slow.
portal-ctl gained record, sheet, frames, anim, poses, and a persistent serve mode. tools/run-checks.sh runs the whole checks/ folder in one session.
remains: a08: land the fling on the cube platform, then finish the chamber.
a09 through the escape maps as scripted playthroughs.
Rocket turrets and the GLaDOS fight.
Turning checks into assertions, rather than 'every command succeeded and the page logged no errors'.
sessions.playthroughNote: The scripted autopilot plays a00 to a07 in order, including the 07a to 07b elevator, and a08 up to the cube platform reaching its east stop. The fling onto the platform still misses. 29 checks all pass.

sessions.title: Test harness
sessions.lede: A new branch off main at 0d06ee2, and a proper test harness first, modelled on Horizon's horizon-ctl. The Linux depot on the box is byte-identical to the older install. escape_02's ending sky came in, and its game logic dropped from 2.0 to 0.3 ms per tick. Turrets were not implemented yet.
landed: tools/portal-ctl.mjs, documented in docs/harness.md: one command per line in, one JSON line per command out, the same exit codes as horizon-ctl. Each run starts its own asset server and headless Chromium. Commands include map, pose, step, shoot, screenshot, bench, diff, state and eval.

Deterministic screenshots: the pause is set before any page code runs, Math.random is seeded, the game only advances on step (fixed 1/66 s ticks), and screenshots are taken from the canvas right after an explicit draw. All 30 later-chamber views were byte-identical between this branch and main at 0d06ee2.
The Linux depot matches the older install already on the box, byte for byte.
2D sky and the sky_camera 3D skybox for maps with sky faces, which is what the escape_02 ending was missing, plus distant scenery.
Animated props are skinned when drawn, not every tick. GLaDOS's body (21,575 vertices) had been CPU-skinned and re-uploaded every 1/66 s tick, on screen or not.
EntityIO.find indexes entities by classname instead of scanning all 1,565 of them. The parenting code looks up each parented prop's parent twice a tick, and escape_02 has 67 of them.

Together those two cuts took escape_02 simulation from 962 to 200 ms per 660 ticks, about 0.3 ms per tick instead of 2.0. A $selfillum-on-models attempt lit GLaDOS's lights but turned a14 and a10's lift platforms bright white, because their textures have no real alpha mask. It was reverted.
sessions.regression: The autopilot playthroughs still finished with the same game times as on 2 Nov: a00 to a01 at 117.8 s, a01 to a02 at 82.0 s, and a03 to a04 at 119.3 s. a02 and a04 timed out when four runs were launched at once, and were not rerun one at a time.
remains: A long-running harness mode (one browser, many commands over a socket) was still ahead; it landed the next morning.
Turrets, and proving animations from recordings rather than single screenshots.
sessions.playthroughNote: Playthrough times were unchanged from 2 Nov, as a check that the harness and the tick-cost cuts did not alter the game.

sessions.title: Portal occlusion and lighting
sessions.lede: The portal shader had left depth undefined, so portals showed through every wall. Walls now hide portals at every recursion level, and a portal behind glass shows through with the glass tint. Props take the room's ambient light instead of a single placeholder brightness, and the white triangle decals around the button pedestals take their light from the floor under them. Frame rate did not change. These four commits, plus the uploader commit, were pushed from the Mac at 8:41 AM EST, which put main at 0d06ee2.
landed: Portals are occluded by nearer geometry and drawn under glass (ab8be38, 7:47 AM EST).
Overlays with no world faces take their light from a coplanar lit face, which is what the white triangle decals around the pedestals needed (6cf43f6).
Models are lit from the BSP leaf ambient cubes, then per vertex (b6fa442, 0d06ee2).
Earlier that morning: an owner-only private R2 bucket for game files, and upload-game-files --s3 for bucket-scoped tokens (8627dd3, a9972e3).
remains: a07 still stopped at the exit switch. a08 and the later chambers were not scripted playthroughs yet.

sessions.title: The port begins
sessions.lede: The Portal port starts. The install was in place at 9:51 AM EST (build 19017868). The first render of the relaxation vault, in headless Chromium with SwiftShader, was at 9:58 AM EST: lightmapped textured brushes, 41 fps at 1024×640, load 460 ms. The first commit, 4091bc3, is at 10:12 AM EST. By 12:32 PM, a00 and a01 play through under the autopilot, and a02 part 1 reaches the middle elevator. Clean-room throughout: Valve Developer Wiki specs and the public Source SDK 2013, no leaked code.
landed: VPK v2 and BSP v20 loaders, a GameFS that follows gameinfo.txt, a lightmapped renderer, and Source-style movement with BSP brush traces.
The game layer: entity I/O, logic entities, triggers, doors, portal-gun placement, recursive stencil portal views, teleport with velocity and view transform, cube pickup, and floor buttons.

func_tracktrain elevators, trigger_changelevel with landmarks, the a01 pedestal gun, MDL skeletal animation, rotating doors, a tumbling cube, overlays, audio (soundscripts, GLaDOS lines and captions), and PVS culling.

tools/autopilot.js walks the maps through the normal controls only (A* over hull traces, aiming and firing the gun the same way the mouse does). a00 reaches a01 at 117.8 s, a01 reaches a02 at 81.8 s, and a02 part 1 reaches the middle elevator at 70.6 s.
remains: a02 part 2: the second box sits in a pit, and the pedestal box is out of reach from the floor.
a03 and everything after.
